newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Investors pour $5.5 bln into Brazil's Parana state.
newsitem.headline: Investors pour $5.5 bln into Brazil's Parana state.

text.p: Brazil's Parana state has attracted some $5.5 billion in investment from local and foreign companies in the last two years, State Governor Jaime Lerner said.

Of this total, 25 percent is coming from automakers, including France's Renault, which is investing $1.0 billion to build a plant in Sao Jose dos Pinhais to produce 30,000 vehicles per year as of 1998.
Lerner revealed the figures after signing a deal with U.S. carmaker Chrysler Corporation to build a $315 million Dakota pickup truck plant in the state.
"I am very happy that the plant will be built here in Campo Largo," he said.
Other investment plans also announced by automakers and auto part manufacturers include Volkswagen-Audi's plant to produce vehicles as of December 1998.
Meanwhile, Detroit Diesel Corporation will make an initial investment of 40 million reais in a plant to build engines, among others.
